chapter: New Orleans bands, brass bands and learning bass
title: Addresses, the Guidry and Allen nightclub before Chicago
summary: Where Garland lived on Cleveland Avenue and Villa Street, and the upstairs club at Guidry and Allen where he played before leaving for Chicago.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: I'm not from downtown. Battlefield. Were you around the battlefield?
When I was here, I was staying. Not when I left there but my people stayed 25 years ago.
And then, you know, I was in the middle of the time.
Yeah, I'm up from downtown.
Battlefield, huh? Were you around the battlefield?
When I was here, I was staying, not when I left there, but my people stayed. 2538 Cleveland Avenue. You know where that's at?
Oh yeah, Gasket Street.
Cleveland Indurgeon Wall. That's where I lived. But when I left, I was staying at 217 South Villa Street.
That's not far from Chinatown, huh?
That's Gaster Street there. Yeah. I was at Villa and Gaster, the continuation of Cleveland Avenue.

Well, they still have the sign on the building there, I think, saying Gasket Street. Yeah? Yeah, it's a ballroom there. It's about, what, about 1400, 1500 block of Gasket. It's still there. You can see Gasket Street on the side of the building. Hmm. You go to the end of the 1400 block, between 14 and 15, and you look around on the building on the Uptown Lake corner. I think that's Villera and Gasket.
That's Villera and Gasket. That must be where, uh...
There was a ballroom there.

Well, what you call them, is that? There's a ballroom on the corner, and upstairs used to be a little club, nightclub. I was playing up there when I left to go to Chicago. Guidry and Allen. Oh. Guidry and Allen.
Fess has told me about that. Hoss told me about that.
Well, that place was Guidry and Allen. Who was Allen?
That was...
There wasn't old man Allen from across the river.
No, no, no. Depend on the place.
Yeah.
Guidry and Allen. No, not Allen over the river. That had the Pacific Brass Band. You talking about Red Howlin's daddy?
Yeah. Mm-hmm.
No, he live in Algiers.
Oh, what?
That was Tom... That's Tom King's building. You know, Tom King's sheriff around here. Not the sheriff. Yeah, he was the sheriff. He was the sheriff.
No, I didn't know him. That was a little before my time. Professor Mineta used to tell me about all those people and places and all that.
Yeah.
